subject.title: [AI] fix(memory): backfill provider.model with resolved model name in…

question: Should OpenClaw accept this source-layer `provider.model` normalization for memory indexes before the broader provider auto-detection work lands?
rationale: The patch appears correct and narrow, but it changes the model identity used for persisted memory metadata and vector lookup when adapters return an empty model, which repository policy treats as compatibility-sensitive.

options.title: Land after upgrade-aware review
options.body: Accept the narrow backfill if maintainers are satisfied that normalizing empty provider models to the resolved configured/default model is the intended upgrade behavior.

options.title: Request full persisted-index proof
options.body: Ask for a live existing-index reindex plus `memory_search` transcript before merge if terminal status and focused tests are not enough for this storage path.

options.title: Pause for broader provider policy
options.body: Hold the PR only if maintainers want the source backfill bundled with the auto-provider migration decision tracked elsewhere.

recommendation.title: Land after upgrade-aware review
recommendation.body: Accept the narrow backfill if maintainers are satisfied that normalizing empty provider models to the resolved configured/default model is the intended upgrade behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: The choice centers on the memory embedding provider-boundary behavior he introduced and repeatedly refactored.
